chunks: And he, peace be upon him, said:
Regarding a man who gave another man money to perform hajj on his behalf, but he performed hajj for himself instead, he said: "It is on behalf of the owner of the money."

key_terms.رَجُلٍ: a man; the legal subject mentioned in the case
key_terms.صَاحِبِ الْمَالِ: the owner of the money; the person for whom the hajj is legally counted
key_terms.عَنْهُ: on his behalf; indicating deputization in worship
key_terms.مَالًا: money; the funds given for performing the hajj
key_terms.نَفْسِهِ: himself; showing that the agent intended the hajj personally
key_terms.يَحُجُّ: to perform hajj; the commissioned act of worship

ai.seo_question: If someone is paid to perform hajj on behalf of another person but performs it for himself, for whom does the hajj count?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about deputized hajj when someone is funded to perform hajj for another person but intends it for himself. The ruling states that the hajj counts for the one who provided the money, highlighting the legal weight of agency and financial authorization in acts of worship.
